Nonchalant

non-shuh-LAHNT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Nonchalant is casually calm and relaxed; unconcerned.

The intern's nonchalant response to spilling coffee on the CEO's laptop -- a shrug and a quick 'oops' -- stunned the whole office.

Worked Example

Even after losing the championship game in the final second, the team captain gave a nonchalant wave to the cameras, as if the outcome barely mattered to him.

Nonchalant describes a casual, unbothered attitude -- the captain isn't hiding devastation, he genuinely seems unconcerned, at least on the surface.

How Nonchalant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

indifferent

indifferent: having no particular interest or concern

offhand

offhand: casual and without much thought or preparation

Antonyms

anxious

anxious: worried or nervous

flustered

flustered: agitated and confused

How Strong Is It? — relaxed → nonchalant → apathetic

relaxed vs. nonchalant

relaxed vs. nonchalant: Relaxed describes general ease, without necessarily downplaying something that should matter.

apathetic vs. nonchalant

apathetic vs. nonchalant: Apathetic describes a deeper, more complete lack of interest or concern -- bordering on not caring about anything at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — non-

prefix — non-: not (Latin)

root — chal-

root — chal-: to care, to be concerned (literally, 'to be warm about') (French chaloir, from Latin calere)

suffix — -ant

suffix — -ant: being in a state of (adjective-forming) (Latin -ans)

Put it together

Put it together: Nonchalant comes from non- ('not') + chaloir ('to care, to matter,' from Latin calere, 'to be warm') + -ant -- literally 'not being warmed up about' something, i.e., unconcerned.

Root Check

Word Choice

Nonchalant describes a general attitude of not caring or not being bothered, often about something that hasn't necessarily caused any real disturbance. That's different from unperturbed, which specifically describes staying calm despite something that would normally cause distress or agitation -- you can be nonchalant about a minor inconvenience without ever having faced a real crisis to stay unperturbed through.
